title: Mitigating Sequential Reappearance in Diffusion Data-Point Unlearning
abstract: arXiv:2609.25166v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Diffusion data-point unlearning is typically evaluated immediately after each deletion, even though subsequent requests may repeatedly update the same model. We identify sequential reappearance, a failure mode in which an instance that is initially judged to be forgotten later returns to the memorized regime without reuse of the deleted data or adversarial fine-tuning. To capture this behavior, we introduce a target-level evaluation protocol that tracks whether each target is forgotten immediately, remains forgotten at the end of the sequence, or reappears during subsequent deletions. We further find that targets that later reappear exhibit sharper local denoising-loss geometry after deletion than targets that remain forgotten.

translated_title: 缓解扩散模型数据点遗忘中的顺序性重现问题
translated_abstract: 扩散模型数据点遗忘通常在每次删除后立即进行评估，即使后续请求可能会反复更新同一个模型。我们识别出了一种称为“顺序性重现”的失效模式：一个最初被判定为已遗忘的实例，在未重新使用被删除数据或进行对抗性微调的情况下，随后又回到了被记忆的状态。为了捕捉这种行为，我们引入了一种目标级别的评估协议，用于跟踪每个目标是立即被遗忘、在序列结束时仍保持遗忘状态，还是在后续删除过程中重新出现。我们进一步发现，后续重现的目标在删除后比保持遗忘状态的目标表现出更尖锐的局部去噪损失几何特性。
tldr: 该论文发现了扩散模型数据点遗忘中的“顺序性重现”失效模式——已遗忘的样本会在后续删除操作中重新被记忆，并提出目标级评估协议来追踪这一现象，同时发现会重现的目标具有更尖锐的局部去噪损失几何特性。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies "sequential reappearance" in diffusion data-point unlearning—where initially forgotten samples re-emerge during subsequent deletions—and introduces a target-level evaluation protocol to track this behavior, finding that reappearing targets exhibit sharper local denoising-loss geometry after deletion.
